units: <cite ref="Pesachim 49b:11">Pes. 49ᵇ</cite> <he>גדולה שנאה ששׂוֹנְאִין וכ׳</he> great is the hatred with which the ignorant hate the scholar, even greater than that which gentiles bear towards Israel.
<cite ref="Pesachim 113b:8">Ib. 113ᵇ</cite> <he>שלשה שׂוֹנְאָן</he> three classes of men does the Lord hate.
<cite ref="Pesachim 113b:8">Ib.</cite> <he>שלשה שונאין זה וכ׳</he> three kinds of creatures hate one another, the dog &c.
<cite ref="Pesachim 113b:6">Ib.</cite> <he>מצוה לִשְׂנֹאתוֹ</he> (Var. <he>מותר</he>) it is right (permitted) to hate him.
<cite ref="Pesachim 113b:5">Ib.</cite> <he>שִׂנְאוּ את אדניכם</he> hate your masters.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 108b:3">Snh. 108ᵇ</cite> the raven said to Noah, <he>רבך שׂוֹנְאֵנִי ואתה שְׂנֵאתַנִי</he> thy master (God) hates me, and thou hatest me.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 1:10">Ab. I, 10</cite> <he>אהוב … ושְׂנָא וכ׳</he> love work and hate office; a. fr.—Part. pass. <cite ref="U01574"><he>שָׂנוּא</he></cite>; f. <he>שְׂנוּאָה</he> &c.

<cite ref="Kiddushin 68a:9">Kidd. 68ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Yevamot 23a:2">Yeb. 23ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 21:15">Deut. XXI, 15</cite>) <he>וכי יש ש׳ לפני המקום וכ׳</he> is there before God a hated one and a beloved one (could it be supposed that the law should allow a discrimination between the children of a favored and of a hated wife)? <cite ref="Deuteronomy 21:15">Ib.</cite> <he>ש׳ בנישואיה</he>, v. <cite ref="N00795"><he>נִישּׂוּאִין</he></cite>; a. e.—Sifra K’doshim, Par. 3, ch. VIII <he>שָׂנְאוּי</he>.

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 4">Num. R. s. 4<sup>8</sup></cite> <he>הר ס̇ינ̇י שבו נִשְׂנְאוּ וכ׳</he> it is called Mount Sinai, because on it the gentiles became hateful to the Lord &c. (v. <cite ref="U01565"><he>שִׂנְאָה</he></cite>); <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 363">Yalk. Is. 363</cite> <he>נִשְׂתַּנְּאוּ</he>.
Taan. 7ᵇ (ref. to ישנא, Koh. VIII, 1) א״ת ישונא אלא יִשָּׂנֵא read not y’shunne (shall be changed), but yissane (shall be hated).
Pesik. R. s. 14 (ref. to Koh. l. c.) יְשׂוּנֶּא יְסוּנֶּה בסמ״ך read y’sunne, with Samekh (v. supra).
